chapter: Germany, Buck's death and ideas about life
title: The book he wants to write on children, marriage and government help
summary: He wants to write about learning life's rules young, argues the law lets 18-year-olds marry without preparation, and says government should finance education and jobs.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

quarter, that's all. I don't want nothing.
See, if I could just teach
the people -- if I could only write a book --
I'm going to try to write a book, I'm trying
to finish mine first but I'm going to write
another book on life -- like something on
life concerning marriage and children, because
that should be something for the people to
learn about the children -- the law is bad
against the children, too, because the law
says you can get married at 18. But that's
all. But look, if you have to learn the left

if you had to learn that in life instead of

be much better off because the children would

Because after you get 18 and get married, here's
what else you've got to do, here's what else
you've got to -- what else -- see what I mean?

But now let's clean up what we dirtied up. We dirtied up mama and papa's life because they had to take care of us until we got big enough. So let's put back in what they had to take out. That should be the children today and of yesterday and the children of tomorrow should have the same idea, because it's set up so bad, so bad.

Look at a boy trying to take care of a wife and his poor mother done scuffled herself to the bone to take care of him to raise him big enough to get married. Now he's going to take care of the wife and in this world her people have done the same thing for her. But she can't stay to help mama get through the things, all the things she got to do, she got to go take care of the things the husband wants to be done.
So look at how all that's separated. It's all mixed up in my book. It don't come out right. I think there should be a law against all the things they got that

there ain't a law against. You get married at 18, but look at what you got to do after you get married. Look, you've got to have money to go to school, you've got to have money after you get out of school, you've got to have money to get a job to set yourself up in any business. Who's going to do that? The government should furnish that for you, too. The government should do that.

When you raise a child to a certain age the government should take over and find a position if necessary for him to get into to manipulate his education or utilize it for him, you know? But it's all so backwards.
